verdict.line: You lose if you trade autos into his stored Grit and eat a full Haymaker; you win if you force him to spend W empty before you commit.

brief.thesis: Sett's passive Haymaker (W) banks every point of damage he takes as Grit, then detonates it as a shield plus true/physical damage punch on cooldowns of 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s. Fiora's whole kit is built around repeated poke-and-dash contact, which means standard Fiora trading directly feeds the ability that makes this matchup lean his way (47.8% win rate over 2,940 games, with lane and solo-kill advantage both his).

theirWindow.when: Right after he lands Knuckle Down (Q) + Facebreaker (E)
theirWindow.what: Q's next two empowered attacks plus a full-side Facebreaker stun (16/14.5/13/11.5/10s cooldown) is his kill window. If you're stuck fighting inside it with your W already on cooldown, disengage rather than trade.

yourWindow.what: Once he's dumped his stored Grit for the shield and punch, he has none banked and W is down for up to 18s at rank 1. That's your window to commit to an extended trade or double-Lunge poke without funding his next shield.

start.why: The 47.4% win rate pick (3,175 games, 89.5% pick rate) gives you the sustain and AD to keep contesting trades Sett is statistically winning early.

boots.why: Taken in 83.1% of games at 48.5% win rate; it directly cuts into Sett's alternating-punch autos and the physical-damage sides of Haymaker.

core.why: Base of every winning Fiora path here; the sustain and AoE on-hit damage let you heal through Haymaker's punch instead of losing the all-in.

Both Eclipse paths outperform the Trinity Force line (57.4% over 310 games, 59.1% over 208 games vs. 51.5% over 672 games); the shield on consecutive hits covers the exact window where Sett's Q empowers his autos.
Pairs with Eclipse for the 59.1% win rate line, over 208 games, giving sustained damage and healing to outlast Sett's missing-health regen from his passive.

you're snowballing and want the burst and move speed proc over Eclipse's defensive shield
the game goes long and you want the ability haste to loop Lunge faster in extended fights
their team stacks hard CC on top of Sett's Facebreaker stun

runes.keystoneWhy: Conqueror's stacking adaptive damage and healing rewards the extended auto-trades you're forced into against Sett's tanky duelist kit. Master-tier Fiora players (19,496 games) instead run Press the Attack, which suits players who want to burn him down fast in a single all-in rather than grind a long trade.

summoners.why: Flash + Ignite is the dominant pick (79.9% pick rate, 47.6% win rate) and the Ignite burn punishes his missing-health regen from Pit Grit. Flash + Barrier (48.7% over fewer games) is the better choice if you expect to be the one all-in'd during his Facebreaker window.

playing.title: Count his Grit before trading
playing.detail: Haymaker (W) stores every point of damage he takes and detonates it as a shield plus true/physical punch. Don't open an extended auto trade until his W is visibly down (18/16.5/15/13.5/12s cooldown) or you're just feeding his next shield.

playing.title: Parry the Knuckle Down follow-up
playing.detail: Riposte (W) blocks his next basic attack and reflects magic damage. Pop it right as he lands Knuckle Down (Q) so one of his two empowered attacks whiffs entirely.

playing.title: Double-Lunge instead of standing autos
playing.detail: Lunge (Q) can be cast twice within a couple seconds for free. Use both dashes to poke damage in and reset range rather than facetanking his alternating punches, since his right punch hits harder and faster.

playing.title: Stay on one side of Facebreaker
playing.detail: Facebreaker (E) only stuns if he pulls enemies from both sides; if you're positioned on just one side you're slowed instead. Watch his approach angle and sidestep so his 490-range pull only catches you alone.

playing.title: Save Burst of Speed for his commit
playing.detail: Burst of Speed (E) ramps your move speed with every attack or Lunge landed while it's active. Hold it until he's already thrown Knuckle Down and Facebreaker so you can either chase a losing fight or disengage a winning one.

playing.title: End trades fast, don't let them linger
playing.detail: Pit Grit heals him harder the lower his health drops, so a fight that drags out as he nears low HP swings back in his favor. Front-load your damage and disengage rather than finishing him off slowly.

playing.title: Hold Blade Waltz for the real all-in
playing.detail: Blade Waltz's repeated hits on the same target deal less damage each time, so its value is the opening burst. Save it to finish a trade once his Grit and cooldowns are empty rather than opening with it.

brief.patchCaveat: Win rates, build paths, runes, and summoner picks above are measured from live games on the current patch via OP.GG; the mechanical reasoning and timing advice are my own reading of the ability text, not measured data.

stats.opponentTip: Do not let Sett activate his (P) by constantly dealing damage with [Q]. Use [W] to block any of his skills to gain the upper hand in combat.
